chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who prays leaning on a staff or leaning against a wall, so he said: 'There is no harm in leaning on a staff and leaning against a wall.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to lean on a staff or wall while praying?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the juristic permissibility (juz') of leaning on a staff or wall during prayer, addressing the practical needs of the weak or ill. It underscores the Shia principle of removing hardship (raf' al-haraj) in worship, ensuring that physical limitations do not invalidate the obligatory act of standing (qiyam).
